Nigeria’s number one player, Canice Abua, is banking on his previous victories over Michael Emmanuel to reach the final of the ongoing Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship in Lagos. Abua faces the country’s third-ranked player in the semi-final on Friday (today), with both players reaching the last four after impressive quarter-final victories at the National Stadium, Surulere. The top seed defeated David Edward 6-3, 6-3, while Emmanuel recorded a 6-2, 6-2 victory over Yaya Sani Inabo to set up the highly anticipated encounter. Abua said his previous meetings with Emmanuel had given him confidence ahead of their latest clash, recalling that he defeated his opponent at the CBN Open in Abuja in May and the Championship Open. “He is a tough opponent, but I always find a way to beat him,” Abua said. I don’t expect anything different in today’s semi-final.” Abua survives scare, Quadre reaches Da-Silva tennis semis Quadre, Abua shine as wheelchair stars enter Da-Silva Open Wheelchair tennis star hails Da-Silva Open inclusion Emmanuel, however, said he remained focused on winning the tournament, insisting that reaching the semi-final had strengthened his belief in his chances of lifting the trophy. “Once you reach the semi-final of a competition, you have a strong chance of winning it all,” he said. “I entered this tournament with a winning mentality, and that hasn’t changed.” Tournament sponsor and former Davis Cup player, Destiny Da-Silva, said the competition had exposed emerging talents capable of improving Nigerian tennis, adding that players needed more opportunities to develop their careers. Da-Silva said the quality of play had improved as competitors advanced, attributing their performances to the prize money and desire to establish themselves among the country’s top players. He said the semi-final matches would be intense contests, with players expected to raise their performances as they approach the final.
